name: Thermocouples and flame sensors
summary: Two-metal probes that make a tiny voltage when heated: gas safety sensors and high-temperature probes.
uses: Replacing a dead pilot sensor on a gas heater or water heater
Measuring stove, kiln or exhaust temperature with a meter
Thermopiles power some gas valves with no outside power
identify: A copper tube or wire whose tip sits in the pilot flame and whose other end screws into the gas valve, in water heaters, furnaces, gas fires and ovens. K-type probes come with multimeters, ovens and kilns. Newer furnaces use a flame rod: a single metal rod with a ceramic collar.
test: Heat the tip in a flame and read millivolts: a gas thermocouple gives roughly 20–35 mV and a thermopile several hundred. A K-type probe reads about 4 mV at 100 °C.

decay.note: Lasts until the tip burns through; spares in drawers last indefinitely.
